items.q: Witnesses caught only a ______ glimpse of the getaway driver before the car sped off down the alley.
items.vi: Các nhân chứng chỉ thoáng thấy tài xế xe tẩu thoát trong chốc lát trước khi chiếc xe lao vụt xuống con hẻm.
items.explanation: Word choice: the clue is only a … glimpse … before the car sped off — a look lasting a split second, so fleeting (passing very quickly) fits. ✗ temporary — lasting a limited time, said of jobs or fixes, not a glimpse; ✗ interim — filling the gap until something permanent (an interim manager); ✗ provisional — arranged for now but likely to change (a provisional booking).

items.q: New officers seldom ______ before their second year, so each is paired with a veteran detective until then.
items.vi: Cảnh sát mới hiếm khi nắm vững công việc trước năm thứ hai, nên mỗi người được ghép cặp với một thám tử kỳ cựu cho đến lúc đó.
items.explanation: Idiom: know the ropes = understand how a job is done; the clue is paired with a veteran … until then — the new officers still need guidance. ✗ pull the strings — secretly control what happens; ✗ call the shots — be the one who makes the decisions; ✗ hold the fort — look after things while the person in charge is away. None describes learning a job.

items.q: After three days of deliberation the jury was still unable to ______ a verdict.
items.vi: Sau ba ngày nghị án, bồi thẩm đoàn vẫn không thể đưa ra được phán quyết.
items.explanation: Collocation: a jury reaches a verdict; the blank is followed directly by a verdict with no preposition, so the verb must be transitive. ✗ arrive — needs at: arrive at a verdict; ✗ come — needs to: come to a verdict; ✗ make — you make a decision, but a verdict is reached, returned or delivered, never made.

items.q: The accused ______ the getaway car that night — he was already in police custody.
items.vi: Bị cáo không thể nào đã lái chiếc xe tẩu thoát đêm đó — lúc ấy anh ta đã bị cảnh sát tạm giữ rồi.
items.explanation: Past deduction: the clue he was already in police custody makes the action impossible, so can't have driven (I am sure he did not). ✗ mustn't have driven — must have deduces that something DID happen; its negative for deduction is can't have, not mustn't have; ✗ needn't have driven — he drove, but it was unnecessary; ✗ shouldn't have driven — he drove, and it was a mistake.

items.q: The rain was ______ all afternoon, stopping and starting so often that the flood sirens were tested three times.
items.vi: Mưa rơi ngắt quãng suốt buổi chiều, ngừng rồi lại rơi thường xuyên đến mức còi báo lũ được thử tới ba lần.
items.explanation: Word choice: the clue stopping and starting so often defines intermittent (happening at irregular intervals, not continuously). ✗ chronic — lasting a long time and hard to cure (a chronic illness, chronic unemployment); ✗ perennial — lasting or returning year after year (a perennial problem); ✗ interim — temporary until something permanent replaces it (an interim government), used of arrangements, not rain.

items.q: Only after the river had burst its banks twice ______ to fund the dredging work.
items.vi: Chỉ sau khi con sông đã tràn bờ hai lần, hội đồng thành phố mới đồng ý cấp kinh phí nạo vét.
items.explanation: Inversion: when a sentence opens with Only after + clause, the main clause takes question order — auxiliary before subject: did the council agree. ✗ the council agreed — normal order is not allowed after a fronted Only after…; ✗ the council did agree — has the auxiliary but no inversion (subject still first); ✗ had the council agreed — inverted, but past perfect belongs to the earlier action (had burst); the agreeing came later, so simple past.

items.q: With no savings to ______, the evicted family spent the winter sleeping in their car.
items.vi: Không có khoản tiết kiệm nào để dựa vào, gia đình bị đuổi khỏi nhà phải ngủ trong xe suốt mùa đông.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: fall back on = rely on something kept in reserve when nothing else is left; the clue is no savings as a safety net. ✗ fall behind with — fail to keep up with payments or work (fall behind with the rent); ✗ fall in with — start mixing with a group, or agree to a plan; ✗ fall out with — quarrel and stop being friends with someone.

items.q: For decades the old seawall has ______ the rising tide ______ bay, but engineers now doubt it can survive another winter.
items.vi: Suốt hàng chục năm, bức tường chắn sóng cũ đã ngăn được thủy triều dâng, nhưng nay các kỹ sư nghi ngờ nó có thể trụ thêm một mùa đông nữa.
items.explanation: Idiom: keep something at bay = stop something dangerous from coming closer; the clue is a seawall holding back the rising tide, and has kept shows a long-running effort. ✗ held / in — hold in means restrain a feeling; in bay is not an expression; ✗ put / to — put to pairs with use, the test, bed, never bay; ✗ set / from — set … from bay exists in no idiom.

items.q: It is high time the city ______ its century-old sewers instead of patching them every monsoon.
items.vi: Đã đến lúc thành phố phải thay hệ thống cống trăm năm tuổi thay vì cứ vá víu mỗi mùa mưa.
items.explanation: Unreal past: after It is high time the verb takes the past subjunctive to say something should already be happening — replaced refers to now, not the past; the clue instead of patching them every monsoon shows the change is overdue. ✗ replaces — present simple is not used after high time; ✗ will replace — no future form after high time; ✗ has replaced — present perfect would mean the sewers are already done, contradicting patching.

items.q: Warnings of the ______ storm surge sent thousands of residents inland before nightfall.
items.vi: Những cảnh báo về đợt nước dâng do bão sắp ập đến khiến hàng nghìn cư dân đổ vào đất liền trước khi trời tối.
items.explanation: Word choice: impending = about to happen, usually something threatening; the clues are warnings and residents fleeing before nightfall. ✗ eventual — happening at the end of a long process (the eventual winner), no sense of danger; ✗ forthcoming — scheduled and expected (the forthcoming election), neutral, not threatening; ✗ subsequent — coming after something already mentioned, but no earlier event is given here.

items.q: Coastal towns that ignored the flood warnings ______ that a seawall costs far less than a rebuild.
items.vi: Những thị trấn ven biển phớt lờ cảnh báo lũ đã phải trả giá đắt để hiểu rằng xây tường chắn sóng rẻ hơn nhiều so với xây dựng lại.
items.explanation: Idiom: learn the hard way = find something out through a painful experience, and it can take a that-clause; the clue is towns that ignored the warnings and paid for it. ✗ took a hard line — adopted a strict, unbending attitude, and cannot be followed by that…; ✗ played hardball — acted aggressively to get their way, no that-clause; ✗ had a hard time — struggled, followed by -ing or with, not that.

items.q: ______ the sheer volume of complaints, the new bus timetable has satisfied almost no one.
items.vi: Xét từ số lượng khiếu nại khổng lồ, lịch chạy xe buýt mới hầu như chẳng làm hài lòng ai.
items.explanation: Participle phrase: judging from (= if one goes by) is a fixed expression whose understood subject is the speaker, who does the judging, so the active -ing form is used regardless of the main subject. ✗ Judged from — passive would make the timetable the thing judged; ✗ Having been judged from — passive and perfect, same problem; ✗ Judge from — a bare verb cannot open a participle clause.

items.q: The documentary set out to ______ public awareness of the smog choking the capital every winter.
items.vi: Bộ phim tài liệu nhằm nâng cao nhận thức của công chúng về màn sương mù ô nhiễm bao trùm thủ đô mỗi mùa đông.
items.explanation: Collocation: raise awareness is the fixed pairing; the clue is the object public awareness right after the blank, so a transitive verb is needed. ✗ rise — intransitive, cannot take an object (awareness rises, but you cannot rise awareness); ✗ lift — collocates with a ban, spirits, restrictions, not awareness; ✗ grow — you grow crops or a business; awareness is raised.

items.q: The housing inspector asked the tenant how long ______ in the damp basement flat.
items.vi: Thanh tra nhà ở hỏi người thuê rằng cô ấy đã sống trong căn hộ tầng hầm ẩm thấp đó bao lâu rồi.
items.explanation: Reported question: after asked … how long the clause keeps statement order and the tense shifts back one step, so she had been living (past perfect continuous). ✗ had she been living — inverted; question order is only for direct questions; ✗ she has been living — present perfect is the direct-speech tense, not backshifted after past asked; ✗ has she been living — both inverted and unshifted.

items.q: The judge ruled that the two prison terms would run ______ rather than one after the other.
items.vi: Thẩm phán phán quyết rằng hai án tù sẽ được thi hành đồng thời chứ không phải nối tiếp nhau.
items.explanation: Word choice: concurrently = at the same time, the legal term for sentences served together; the clue is the contrast with rather than one after the other. ✗ contemporarily — belonging to the same period or the present era, not used for running sentences; ✗ coincidentally — by chance, at the same time by accident; ✗ instantaneously — immediately, in an instant, says nothing about overlap.

items.q: Once the most feared prosecutor in the city, she seems to have ______ — her last three cases collapsed within a week.
items.vi: Từng là công tố viên đáng sợ nhất thành phố, giờ bà dường như đã mất đi sự sắc bén — ba vụ gần nhất của bà đều đổ vỡ trong vòng một tuần.
items.explanation: Idiom: lose your touch = no longer have the skill you once had; the clue is once the most feared … her last three cases collapsed. ✗ lost her head — panicked and stopped thinking clearly; ✗ lost her voice — literal, could not speak (a sore throat); ✗ lost her footing — slipped and fell, or briefly lost her balance or position — not a lasting decline in skill.

items.q: Residents of the tower block rarely speak to ______, even after years on the same floor.
items.vi: Cư dân tòa chung cư hiếm khi trò chuyện với nhau, dù đã sống cùng tầng nhiều năm.
items.explanation: Reciprocal pronoun: one another (= each other) shows that the residents act on each other; the clue is the plural subject residents doing something mutual. ✗ each other's — possessive form, needs a noun after it (each other's names); ✗ themselves — reflexive, would mean each resident talks to himself or herself; ✗ the other — singular, refers to one specific second person out of two.

items.q: The jury foreman refused to ______ the majority verdict until every doubt had been discussed.
items.vi: Chủ tịch bồi thẩm đoàn từ chối tán thành phán quyết của đa số cho đến khi mọi nghi vấn đã được thảo luận.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: go along with = accept or agree to a decision; the clue is refused … until every doubt had been discussed — he would not accept the verdict yet. ✗ go in for — enjoy or take part in (go in for competitions); ✗ go down with — fall ill with (go down with flu); ✗ go off with — take something away or run off with someone.

items.q: The clinic now opens at six in the morning ______ shift workers can be seen before they start work.
items.vi: Phòng khám nay mở cửa từ sáu giờ sáng để công nhân làm ca có thể được khám trước khi vào làm.
items.explanation: Purpose clause: so that introduces a full clause with its own subject and verb — here shift workers can be seen. ✗ in order to — must be followed by a bare infinitive (in order to see), not subject + verb; ✗ so as to — same, infinitive only; ✗ in case — expresses a precaution against something that might happen, not the aim of opening early.

items.q: Small farmers along the delta will ______ the brunt of the new export tariffs, according to the ministry's own forecast.
items.vi: Theo chính dự báo của bộ, các nông hộ nhỏ dọc vùng châu thổ sẽ phải gánh chịu nặng nề nhất từ mức thuế xuất khẩu mới.
items.explanation: Collocation: bear the brunt of = suffer the worst part of something; the clue is the fixed noun the brunt, which takes only bear. ✗ carry — carry the burden / the can, but not the brunt; ✗ hold — hold a grudge / the line, no pairing with brunt; ✗ stand — stand the strain / the pressure, again not brunt.

items.q: The witness admitted ______ the accused leave the warehouse, but denied having spoken to him.
items.vi: Nhân chứng thừa nhận đã thấy bị cáo rời khỏi nhà kho, nhưng phủ nhận việc đã nói chuyện với anh ta.
items.explanation: Verb pattern: admit takes a gerund, and the perfect gerund having seen shows the seeing happened before the admission; the parallel clue is denied having spoken. ✗ to see — admit is never followed by a to-infinitive; ✗ to have seen — perfect infinitive, still an infinitive, so wrong after admit; ✗ see — a bare infinitive follows only modals or verbs like make/let.

items.q: The residents' committee only ______ round to ______ the leaking roof after part of the ceiling had collapsed.
items.vi: Ban đại diện cư dân chỉ chịu bắt tay vào sửa mái dột sau khi một phần trần nhà đã sập.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: get round to + -ing = finally find time for something you have put off; the clue is only … after part of the ceiling had collapsed. ✗ set / repairing — set round to does not exist (set about + -ing would); ✗ got / repair — the to in get round to is a preposition, so a gerund must follow, not a bare verb; ✗ put / repair — put round to is not a phrasal verb.

items.q: Developers complain that the planning department keeps ______, adding fresh conditions every time a scheme is resubmitted.
items.vi: Các nhà phát triển phàn nàn rằng sở quy hoạch cứ liên tục thay đổi luật chơi, thêm điều kiện mới mỗi lần hồ sơ được nộp lại.
items.explanation: Idiom: move the goalposts = unfairly change the rules while something is already under way; the clue is adding fresh conditions every time a scheme is resubmitted. ✗ moving heaven and earth — making every possible effort to achieve something; ✗ moving with the times — modernising, keeping up with change; ✗ moving mountains — achieving something that seemed impossible.

items.q: The inquiry published an ______ report on the landfill fire while the full investigation continues.
items.vi: Ủy ban điều tra đã công bố báo cáo sơ bộ về vụ cháy bãi rác trong khi cuộc điều tra đầy đủ vẫn đang tiếp diễn.
items.explanation: Word choice: an interim report is issued in the meantime, before the final one; the clue is while the full investigation continues. ✗ instant — happening immediately (instant coffee, an instant reply), does not describe a report; ✗ momentary — lasting only a moment (a momentary pause); ✗ transitory — passing, not lasting (transitory fame), about duration, not a stage in a process.

items.q: Hardly anyone on the estate bothers to sort their recycling, ______?
items.vi: Hầu như chẳng ai trong khu dân cư chịu phân loại rác tái chế, phải không?
items.explanation: Question tag: hardly makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive; and anyone is referred back to with plural they: do they. ✗ don't they — negative tag on an already negative statement; ✗ does he — anyone takes they, not he; ✗ doesn't it — wrong pronoun and wrong polarity.
